items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: one of the bands that I worked with in my young years which was so important to me which was George Barnes and Ruby Braff, the quartet record.

ctx.x: I really enjoy hearing a combo or small ensemble that is basically a jazz unit but every once in a while they’ll do something that you know has been arranged and rehearsed. I think it really adds a lot of the performance that that group took the time to do that.
I feel the same way. Like T.S. Monk’s band, you know Thelonious Monk Junior, I mean I heard them and they have arrangements and they’re not reading music, they have their © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

act together. And the improvisation is very good, but there are a lot of great improvisers around nowadays, but there are very few bands. And my looking back in history, I mean I grew up with the Nat Cole Trio. My father had a trio based like that, on that kind of thing, and those tight arrangements. And Benny Goodman’s trios and quartets and all the groups that I admired as I grew up were very well thought out and very well rehearsed, and the improvisation was a great part of it but so were the arrangements.…
